spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
spec.summary:
A compact, single-player bubble-wrap popping experience centered on one reusable 4-by-4 sheet with 16 individually pressable bubbles. The player spawns beside a safe, collidable tabletop station with the entire sheet immediately visible at close range. A short visual cue and minimal instruction invite a mouse click or touch tap. Each valid press visibly compresses one bubble, reaches a distinct pop moment with synchronized Marketplace audio, settles into a clearly collapsed state, and only then increases the counter by exactly one. Locked per-bubble state prevents holds, rapid repeats, overlapping inputs, and already-popped bubbles from scoring again. After all 16 bubbles are popped, completion feedback appears and a deliberate reset control creates a fresh unpopped sheet and returns the counter to zero.

The shared world is confined to Workspace/Forge_4692609c69a4 and consists of a small bounded tabletop vignette, a safe spawn, the central interaction sheet, and restrained supporting props or lighting. Server-owned state validates bubble identity, interaction distance, current phase, completion state, and request rate; the client owns device input and presentation while treating replicated state as authoritative. No saving, purchases, progression, multiplayer-specific competition, or large traversal space will be added. Respawn restores input and HUD bindings without duplicating interfaces or resetting the active sheet unexpectedly.

Marketplace discovery and inspection occur before replacement implementation. A complete reusable bubble-wrap interaction is preferred and must be audited for geometry, scripts, animation, input behavior, state handling, and embedded sound references. Only verified missing integration may be authored after that inspection. A separately declared Marketplace audio requirement remains mandatory even when the sound is captured from the retained component. Assumed defaults are 16 bubbles, a short approximately 0.15–0.30 second visible press/pop/settle sequence, a persistent collapsed final state, and a compact two-step reset confirmation to make reset deliberate. All interaction, audio, animation, exact-counting, completion, reset, desktop, and touch claims require observed native gameplay verification rather than code inspection.
spec.visualDirection:
Present the game as a close, softly lit tabletop ASMR vignette rather than an open map. The bubble sheet is the dominant focal object, centered on a warm matte wood or neutral craft surface and sized so all 16 bubbles remain readable from the starting view. Keep the spawn within roughly 6–8 studs of the interaction area, with a collidable floor and unobtrusive boundaries that prevent falling or wandering away. A desk lamp silhouette, shallow tray edge, or one restrained stationery grouping may frame the sheet, but decoration must not obscure bubble hit targets or compete with the interaction.

Use a calm hierarchy: warm low-saturation table and background colors, a translucent or pale cool-toned bubble sheet, brighter specular highlights on intact domes, and darker/flatter collapsed bubbles. Intact, pressing, popping, and popped states must be distinguishable through silhouette and height, not color alone. The press phase should show immediate downward travel or compression; the pop moment should have a crisp collapse and restrained highlight response; the settle phase should end in a stable recessed shape without regrowing the bubble. Completion can use a brief sheet-wide glow, soft border pulse, or concise banner, avoiding confetti or noisy effects that undermine the ASMR tone.

The HUD should occupy little screen space: a high-contrast counter such as “Popped 0 / 16” and one reset button in a safe corner, with touch-sized controls, restrained rounded panels, and no inventory or economy chrome. The reset confirmation should appear adjacent to the same control instead of opening a large modal. Input hover or selection feedback on desktop and clear touch-down feedback on mobile should identify the targeted bubble without delaying the physical response. Camera composition must keep the sheet close and legible while preserving normal device aspect ratios and avoiding GUI overlap.

Backup:findFirstChild(Button.Name):remove()
Active = true

function Regen()
	if RemovesPreviousModel == true then
		local PreviousModel = Button.Parent:children()
		for i = 1, #PreviousModel do
			if PreviousModel[i] ~= Button then
				PreviousModel[i]:Destroy()
			end
		end
	end
	local Clone = Backup:clone()
	local Children = Clone:children()
	for i = 1, #Children do
		Children[i].Parent = Button.Parent
		if Children[i]:isA("BasePart") == true or Children[i]:isA("Model") == true then
			Children[i]:makeJoints()
		end
	end
	Clone:Destroy()
end

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local part = script.Parent
local clickDetector = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("ClickDetector")
local popSound = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("Sound")
local mesh = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")

local originalSize = mesh and mesh.Scale or Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
local originalTransparency = part.Transparency
local originalColor = part.Color

part:SetAttribute("Popped", false)
part:SetAttribute("State", "Intact")

local isBusy = false

local function onReset()
	isBusy = false
	part:SetAttribute("Popped", false)
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Intact")
	if clickDetector then
		clickDetector.MaxActivationDistance = 32
	end
	if mesh then
		mesh.Scale = originalSize
	end
	part.Transparency = originalTransparency
	part.Color = originalColor
end

local function onPop(player)
	if isBusy or part:GetAttribute("Popped") == true then
		return
	end
	isBusy = true
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Pressing")
	if clickDetector then
		clickDetector.MaxActivationDistance = 0
	end

	-- Phase 1: Visible depression
	if mesh then
		local depressTween = TweenService:Create(mesh, TweenInfo.new(0.08, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In), {
			Scale = Vector3.new(originalSize.X * 1.1, originalSize.Y * 0.4, originalSize.Z * 1.1)
		})
		depressTween:Play()
		depressTween.Completed:Wait()
	else
		task.wait(0.08)
	end

	-- Phase 2: Distinct pop moment with synchronized audio
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Popping")
	if popSound then
		popSound:Play()
	end

	-- Phase 3: Settle into recessed collapsed state
	if mesh then
		local settleTween = TweenService:Create(mesh, TweenInfo.new(0.12, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
			Scale = Vector3.new(originalSize.X * 0.9, originalSize.Y * 0.15, originalSize.Z * 0.9)
		})
		settleTween:Play()
		settleTween.Completed:Wait()
	else
		task.wait(0.12)
	end

	part.Transparency = math.clamp(originalTransparency + 0.35, 0, 0.85)
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Popped")
	part:SetAttribute("Popped", true)
	isBusy = false
end
	if clickDetector then
	clickDetector.MouseClick:Connect(onPop)
end

	-- Waits for a child to appear. Not efficient, but it shoudln't have to be. It helps with debugging.

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local part = script.Parent
local clickDetector = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("ClickDetector")
local popSound = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("Sound")
local mesh = part:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")

local originalSize = mesh and mesh.Scale or Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
local originalTransparency = part.Transparency
local originalColor = part.Color

part:SetAttribute("Popped", false)
part:SetAttribute("State", "Intact")

local isBusy = false

local function onReset()
	isBusy = false
	part:SetAttribute("Popped", false)
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Intact")
	if clickDetector then
		clickDetector.MaxActivationDistance = 32
	end
	if mesh then
		mesh.Scale = originalSize
	end
	part.Transparency = originalTransparency
	part.Color = originalColor
end

local function onPop(player)
	if isBusy or part:GetAttribute("Popped") == true then
		return
	end
	isBusy = true
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Pressing")
	if clickDetector then
		clickDetector.MaxActivationDistance = 0
	end

	-- Phase 1: Visible depression
	if mesh then
		local depressTween = TweenService:Create(mesh, TweenInfo.new(0.08, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In), {
			Scale = Vector3.new(originalSize.X * 1.1, originalSize.Y * 0.4, originalSize.Z * 1.1)
		})
		depressTween:Play()
		depressTween.Completed:Wait()
	else
		task.wait(0.08)
	end

	-- Phase 2: Distinct pop moment with synchronized audio
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Popping")
	if popSound then
		popSound:Play()
	end

	-- Phase 3: Settle into recessed collapsed state
	if mesh then
		local settleTween = TweenService:Create(mesh, TweenInfo.new(0.12, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
			Scale = Vector3.new(originalSize.X * 0.9, originalSize.Y * 0.15, originalSize.Z * 0.9)
		})
		settleTween:Play()
		settleTween.Completed:Wait()
	else
		task.wait(0.12)
	end

	part.Transparency = math.clamp(originalTransparency + 0.35, 0, 0.85)
	part:SetAttribute("State", "Popped")
	part:SetAttribute("Popped", true)
	isBusy = false
end
	if clickDetector then
	clickDetector.MouseClick:Connect(onPop)
end

part:GetAttributeChangedSignal("ResetTrigger"):Connect(onReset)
